questions.text:
Let R be a relation defined on the set $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}\times\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ by
$R=\{((a, b), (c, d)) : 2a+3b=3c+4d\}$.
Then the number of elements in R is
questions.sol:
$2a+3b=3c+4d \iff 2(a-2d)=3(c-b)$, so $a-2d$ is a multiple of 3 and $c-b=\dfrac{2(a-2d)}{3}$.
With $a,d\in\{1,\ldots,4\}$, $a-2d\in\{-7,\ldots,2\}$, so $a-2d\in\{-6,-3,0\}$, giving $c-b\in\{-4,-2,0\}$; $-4$ is impossible.
$a-2d=0$: $(a,d)=(2,1),(4,2)$ with $c=b$ (4 ways): 8 elements.
$a-2d=-3$: $(a,d)=(1,2),(3,3)$ with $c=b-2$, $b\in\{3,4\}$: 4 elements.
Total $=12$.

questions.text:
If the domain of the function
$f(x)=\log_{(10x^2-17x+7)}\left(18x^2-11x+1\right)$
is $(-\infty, a)\cup(b, c)\cup(d, \infty)-\{e\}$, then
$90(a+b+c+d+e)$ equals:
questions.sol:
Base positive: $(10x-7)(x-1)>0 \Rightarrow x<\dfrac{7}{10}$ or $x>1$.
Argument positive: $(9x-1)(2x-1)>0 \Rightarrow x<\dfrac19$ or $x>\dfrac12$.
Base $\neq1$: $10x^2-17x+6=0 \Rightarrow x=\dfrac12,\ \dfrac65$.
Domain $=\left(-\infty,\dfrac19\right)\cup\left(\dfrac12,\dfrac{7}{10}\right)\cup(1,\infty)-\left\{\dfrac65\right\}$.
$90\left(\dfrac19+\dfrac12+\dfrac7{10}+1+\dfrac65\right)=10+45+63+90+108=316$.

Then $\displaystyle\sum_{z\in S}|z|^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$|z-6i|=|z-2i|$: $z$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $6i$ and $2i$, so $\operatorname{Im}z=4$. Let $z=x+4i$.
$25\left[(x-8)^2+36\right]=9\left(x^2+36\right) \Rightarrow 16x^2-400x+2176=0 \Rightarrow x^2-25x+136=0 \Rightarrow x=8$ or $17$.
$\sum|z|^2=(64+16)+(289+16)=385$.

questions.text:
The number of the real solutions of the equation:
$x|x+3|+|x-1|-2=0$ is
questions.sol:
$x\ge1$: $x^2+4x-3=0 \Rightarrow x=-2\pm\sqrt7$; neither is $\ge1$.
$-3\le x<1$: $x^2+2x-1=0 \Rightarrow x=-1\pm\sqrt2$; both lie in the interval.
$x<-3$: $-x^2-4x-1=0 \Rightarrow x=-2\pm\sqrt3$; only $-2-\sqrt3$ lies in the interval.
Number of real solutions $=3$.

Consider an A.P.: $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$; $a_1>0$. If $a_2-a_1=\dfrac{-3}{4}$, $a_n=\dfrac{1}{4}a_1$, and
$\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i=\dfrac{525}{2}$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{17}a_i$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$a_1-\dfrac34(n-1)=\dfrac{a_1}{4} \Rightarrow a_1=n-1$.
$\dfrac n2\left(a_1+\dfrac{a_1}4\right)=\dfrac{5n(n-1)}{8}=\dfrac{525}{2} \Rightarrow n(n-1)=420 \Rightarrow n=21$, $a_1=20$.
$\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{17}a_i=\dfrac{17}{2}\left(40+16\left(-\dfrac34\right)\right)=\dfrac{17}{2}\times28=238$.

questions.text: From a lot containing 10 defective and 90 non-defective bulbs, 8 bulbs are selected one by one with replacement. Then the probability of getting at least 7 defective bulbs is
questions.sol:
Each draw is defective with probability $p=\dfrac1{10}$, independently (binomial, $n=8$).
$P(X\ge7)=\binom87\left(\dfrac1{10}\right)^7\dfrac9{10}+\left(\dfrac1{10}\right)^8=\dfrac{72+1}{10^8}=\dfrac{73}{10^8}$.

Let each of the two ellipses $E_1:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1, (a>b)$ and
$E_2:\dfrac{x^2}{A^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{B^2}=1, (A
questions.sol:
$E_1$: $2ae=8 \Rightarrow a=5$, $b^2=a^2(1-e^2)=9$, $l_1=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{18}{5}$.
$9l_2=2l_1^2=\dfrac{648}{25} \Rightarrow l_2=\dfrac{72}{25}$.
$E_2$ (major axis along $y$): $A^2=B^2(1-e^2)=\dfrac{9B^2}{25}$, $l_2=\dfrac{2A^2}{B}=\dfrac{18B}{25}=\dfrac{72}{25} \Rightarrow B=4$.
Distance between foci $=2Be=8\times\dfrac45=\dfrac{32}{5}$.

questions.text: Let a circle of radius 4 pass through the origin O, the points $A\left(-\sqrt{3}a, 0\right)$ and $B\left(0, -\sqrt{2}b\right)$, where $a$ and $b$ are real parameters and $ab\neq0$. Then the locus of the centroid of $\Delta OAB$ is a circle of radius
questions.sol:
$\angle AOB=90^\circ$, so AB is a diameter: $AB^2=3a^2+2b^2=8^2=64$.
Centroid $(h,k)=\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt3a}{3},-\dfrac{\sqrt2b}{3}\right)$, so $3a^2=9h^2$ and $2b^2=9k^2$.
$9(h^2+k^2)=64 \Rightarrow h^2+k^2=\left(\dfrac83\right)^2$: radius $\dfrac83$.

questions.text:
If $\cot x=\dfrac{5}{12}$ for some $x\in\left(\pi, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$, then
$\sin7x\left(\cos\dfrac{13x}{2}+\sin\dfrac{13x}{2}\right)+\cos7x\left(\cos\dfrac{13x}{2}-\sin\dfrac{13x}{2}\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Regroup: $\left(\sin7x\cos\dfrac{13x}2-\cos7x\sin\dfrac{13x}2\right)+\left(\cos7x\cos\dfrac{13x}2+\sin7x\sin\dfrac{13x}2\right)=\sin\dfrac x2+\cos\dfrac x2$.
In the third quadrant $\cos x=-\dfrac5{13}$, and $\dfrac x2\in\left(\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac{3\pi}4\right)$.
$\sin\dfrac x2=\sqrt{\dfrac{1+\frac5{13}}2}=\dfrac3{\sqrt{13}}$, $\cos\dfrac x2=-\sqrt{\dfrac{1-\frac5{13}}2}=-\dfrac2{\sqrt{13}}$.
Value $=\dfrac1{\sqrt{13}}$.

questions.text: Let $A(1, 0)$, $B(2, -1)$ and $C\left(\dfrac{7}{3}, \dfrac{4}{3}\right)$ be three points. If the equation of the bisector of the angle ABC is $\alpha x+\beta y=5$, then the value of $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is
questions.sol:
$\vec{BA}=(-1,1)$, $|BA|=\sqrt2$; $\vec{BC}=\left(\dfrac13,\dfrac73\right)$, $|BC|=\dfrac{5\sqrt2}{3}$.
Sum of unit vectors: $\dfrac{(-1,1)}{\sqrt2}+\dfrac{(1,7)}{5\sqrt2}=\dfrac{(-4,12)}{5\sqrt2}$, direction $(-1,3)$.
Line through $(2,-1)$ with direction $(-1,3)$: $3x+y=5$. So $\alpha=3$, $\beta=1$ and $\alpha^2+\beta^2=10$.

questions.text: The value of $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cosec}20^\circ-\sec20^\circ}{\cos20^\circ\cos40^\circ\cos60^\circ\cos80^\circ}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Numerator: $\dfrac{\sqrt3\cos20^\circ-\sin20^\circ}{\sin20^\circ\cos20^\circ}=\dfrac{2\sin40^\circ}{\frac12\sin40^\circ}=4$.
Denominator: $\cos20^\circ\cos40^\circ\cos80^\circ=\dfrac18$, times $\cos60^\circ=\dfrac12$, gives $\dfrac1{16}$.
Value $=4\times16=64$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{c}=\vec{a}\times\vec{b}$. Let $\vec{d}$ be a vector such that $\left|\vec{d}-\vec{a}\right|=\sqrt{11}$, $\left|\vec{c}\times\vec{d}\right|=3$ and the angle between $\vec{c}$ and $\vec{d}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. Then $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\vec c=\vec a\times\vec b=2\hat i-2\hat j+\hat k$, $|\vec c|=3$.
$|\vec c\times\vec d|=3|\vec d|\sin\dfrac\pi4=3 \Rightarrow |\vec d|=\sqrt2$.
$|\vec d-\vec a|^2=|\vec d|^2+|\vec a|^2-2\vec a\cdot\vec d \Rightarrow 11=2+9-2\vec a\cdot\vec d \Rightarrow \vec a\cdot\vec d=0$.

questions.text:
Let the lines $L_1:\vec{r}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}+\lambda\left(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\right), \lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ and
$L_2:\vec{r}=\left(4\hat{i}+\hat{j}\right)+\mu\left(5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right), \mu\in\mathbb{R}$, intersect at the point R. Let P and Q be the points lying on lines $L_1$ and $L_2$, respectively, such that $\left|\overline{PR}\right|=\sqrt{29}$ and $\left|\overline{PQ}\right|=\sqrt{\dfrac{47}{3}}$. If the point P lies in the first octant, then $27(QR)^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Equating: $1+2\lambda=4+5\mu$, $2+3\lambda=1+2\mu$, $3+4\lambda=\mu$ give $\lambda=\mu=-1$, so $R=(-1,-1,-1)$.
$|\overrightarrow{PR}|=\sqrt{29}=|(2,3,4)|$, so $P=R\pm(2,3,4)$; first octant gives $P=(1,2,3)$.
Let $Q=R+s(5,2,1)$. $PQ^2=|s(5,2,1)-(2,3,4)|^2=30s^2-40s+29=\dfrac{47}3 \Rightarrow 9s^2-12s+4=0 \Rightarrow s=\dfrac23$.
$QR^2=30s^2=\dfrac{40}3$, so $27\,QR^2=360$.

questions.text: If the function $f(x)=\dfrac{e^x\left(e^{\tan x-x}-1\right)+\log_e(\sec x+\tan x)-x}{\tan x-x}$ is continuous at $x=0$, then the value of $f(0)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$e^x\left(e^{\tan x-x}-1\right)=e^{\tan x}-e^x$, and $\dfrac{e^{\tan x}-e^x}{\tan x-x}=e^x\cdot\dfrac{e^{\tan x-x}-1}{\tan x-x}\to1$.
Near 0: $\log_e(\sec x+\tan x)=x+\dfrac{x^3}6+\ldots$ and $\tan x-x=\dfrac{x^3}3+\ldots$, so the second part $\to\dfrac{1/6}{1/3}=\dfrac12$.
$f(0)=1+\dfrac12=\dfrac32$.

questions.text:
Let $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbb{R}$ be such that the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}2\alpha\left(x^2-2\right)+2\beta x, & x<1\\(\alpha+3)x+(\alpha-\beta), & x\ge1\end{cases}$
be differentiable at all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Then $34(\alpha+\beta)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Continuity at 1: $-2\alpha+2\beta=2\alpha+3-\beta \Rightarrow 3\beta-4\alpha=3$.
Equal derivatives at 1: $4\alpha+2\beta=\alpha+3 \Rightarrow 3\alpha+2\beta=3$.
Solving: $\alpha=\dfrac3{17}$, $\beta=\dfrac{21}{17}$, so $34(\alpha+\beta)=34\times\dfrac{24}{17}=48$.

questions.text:
Let $f(t)=\displaystyle\int\left(\dfrac{1-\sin(\log_e t)}{1-\cos(\log_e t)}\right)dt,\ t>1$.
If $f\left(e^{\pi/2}\right)=-e^{\pi/2}$ and $f\left(e^{\pi/4}\right)=\alpha e^{\pi/4}$, then $\alpha$ equals
questions.sol:
Put $t=e^u$: $f=\displaystyle\int e^u\,\dfrac{1-\sin u}{1-\cos u}\,du=\int e^u\left(\dfrac12\operatorname{cosec}^2\dfrac u2-\cot\dfrac u2\right)du$.
With $g(u)=-\cot\dfrac u2$, $g'(u)=\dfrac12\operatorname{cosec}^2\dfrac u2$, so the integrand is $e^u(g+g')$ and $f=-e^u\cot\dfrac u2+C$.
$f\left(e^{\pi/2}\right)=-e^{\pi/2}+C=-e^{\pi/2} \Rightarrow C=0$.
$f\left(e^{\pi/4}\right)=-e^{\pi/4}\cot\dfrac\pi8=-\left(1+\sqrt2\right)e^{\pi/4}$, so $\alpha=-1-\sqrt2$.

questions.text: Let $A_1$ be the bounded area enclosed by the curves $y=x^2+2$, $x+y=8$ and $y$-axis that lies in the first quadrant. Let $A_2$ be the bounded area enclosed by the curves $y=x^2+2$, $y^2=x$, $x=2$, and $y$-axis that lies in the first quadrant. Then $A_1-A_2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$x^2+2=8-x \Rightarrow x=2$. $A_1=\displaystyle\int_0^2\left(6-x-x^2\right)dx=12-2-\dfrac83=\dfrac{22}3$.
$A_2=\displaystyle\int_0^2\left(x^2+2-\sqrt x\right)dx=\dfrac83+4-\dfrac{4\sqrt2}3=\dfrac{20-4\sqrt2}{3}$.
$A_1-A_2=\dfrac{2+4\sqrt2}3=\dfrac23\left(2\sqrt2+1\right)$.

questions.text: The number of $3\times2$ matrices A, which can be formed using the elements of the set $\{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2\}$ such that the sum of all the diagonal elements of $A^TA$ is 5, is __________
questions.sol:
$\operatorname{tr}(A^TA)$ is the sum of the squares of all 6 entries, and each square is 0, 1 or 4.
Sum 5 = $4+1$: choose the positions of $\pm2$ and $\pm1$ ($6\times5$) and signs ($4$): $120$.
Sum 5 = five 1s: choose the zero entry (6) and signs ($2^5$): $192$.
Total $=312$.

questions.text: The number of numbers greater than 5000, less than 9000 and divisible by 3, that can be formed using the digits 0, 1, 2, 5, 9, if the repetition of the digits is allowed, is __________
questions.sol:
The numbers have 4 digits and must start with 5 (a leading 9 gives at least 9000).
Since $5\equiv2 \pmod 3$, the last three digits must have sum $\equiv1 \pmod 3$. Residues: $\{0,9\}\to0$, $\{1\}\to1$, $\{2,5\}\to2$.
Count triples by residues $(r_1,r_2,r_3)$ with sum $\equiv1$: patterns $\{0,0,1\}$: $3\times2\times2\times1=12$; $\{1,1,2\}$: $3\times1\times1\times2=6$; $\{0,2,2\}$: $3\times2\times2\times2=24$.
Total $=12+6+24=42$.

questions.text: Let a line L passing through the point $P(1,1,1)$ be perpendicular to the lines $\dfrac{x-4}{4}=\dfrac{y-1}{1}=\dfrac{z-1}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x-17}{1}=\dfrac{y-71}{1}=\dfrac{z}{0}$. Let the line L intersect the $yz$-plane at the point Q. Another line parallel to L and passing through the point $S(1, 0, -1)$ intersects the $yz$-plane at the point R. Then the square of the area of the parallelogram PQRS is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Direction of L: $(4,1,1)\times(1,1,0)=(-1,1,3)$.
L: $(1-t,1+t,1+3t)$ meets $x=0$ at $t=1$: $Q=(0,2,4)$. The parallel line through S gives $R=(0,1,2)$.
$\overrightarrow{PQ}=(-1,1,3)$, $\overrightarrow{PS}=(0,-1,-2)$, $\overrightarrow{PQ}\times\overrightarrow{PS}=(1,-2,1)$.
Area$^2=1+4+1=6$.

questions.text:
Let $(2\alpha, \alpha)$ be the largest interval in which the function $f(t)=\dfrac{|t+1|}{t^2}$, $t<0$, is strictly decreasing. Then the local maximum value of the function
$g(x)=2\log_e(x-2)+\alpha x^2+4x-\alpha$, $x>2$, is __________
questions.sol:
For $t<-1$, $f=-\dfrac{t+1}{t^2}$ and $f'(t)=\dfrac{t+2}{t^3}$, which is negative only for $-20$.
So the interval is $(-2,-1)$ and $\alpha=-1$.
$g(x)=2\log_e(x-2)-x^2+4x+1$, $g'(x)=\dfrac2{x-2}-2(x-2)=0 \Rightarrow x=3$ (a maximum since $g''<0$).
$g(3)=0-9+12+1=4$.

questions.text:
Let a differentiable function $f$ satisfy the equation $\displaystyle\int_0^{36}f\left(\dfrac{tx}{36}\right)dt=4\alpha f(x)$.
If $y=f(x)$ is a standard parabola passing through the points $(2, 1)$ and $(-4, \beta)$, then $\beta^{\alpha}$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Put $u=\dfrac{tx}{36}$: $\dfrac{36}{x}\displaystyle\int_0^x f(u)\,du=4\alpha f(x)$.
A standard parabola $y=f(x)$ is $f(x)=kx^2$: $\dfrac{36}{x}\cdot\dfrac{kx^3}{3}=12kx^2=4\alpha kx^2 \Rightarrow \alpha=3$.
Through $(2,1)$: $k=\dfrac14$, so $\beta=f(-4)=4$ and $\beta^\alpha=4^3=64$.

questions.sol: For a spring, $kL$ is constant. The smaller piece has length $\dfrac L4$, so $k=4\times15=60$ N/m.

questions.text: Two resistors 2 $\Omega$ and 3 $\Omega$ are connected in the gaps of bridge as shown in figure. The null point is obtained with the contact of jockey at some point on wire $XY$. When an unknown resistor is connected in parallel with 3 $\Omega$ resistor, the null point is shifted by 22.5 cm toward $Y$. The resistance of unknown resistor is __________ $\Omega$.
questions.sol:
Metre bridge (100 cm wire): $\dfrac23=\dfrac{l}{100-l} \Rightarrow l=40$ cm.
New balance at $l=62.5$ cm: $\dfrac{2}{R'}=\dfrac{62.5}{37.5}=\dfrac53 \Rightarrow R'=1.2\ \Omega$.
$\dfrac{3R}{3+R}=1.2 \Rightarrow 1.8R=3.6 \Rightarrow R=2\ \Omega$.

questions.text:
Three masses 200 kg, 300 kg and 400 kg are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle with sides 20 m. They are rearranged on the vertices of a bigger triangle of side 25 m and with the same centre. The work done in this process __________ J.
(Gravitational constant $G=6.7\times10^{-11}$ N m$^2$/ kg$^2$)
questions.sol:
$U=-\dfrac{G}{a}\left(m_1m_2+m_2m_3+m_3m_1\right)$, with $\sum m_im_j=60000+120000+80000=2.6\times10^5$ kg$^2$.
$W=U_f-U_i=G\times2.6\times10^5\left(\dfrac1{20}-\dfrac1{25}\right)=6.7\times10^{-11}\times2.6\times10^5\times0.01\approx1.74\times10^{-7}$ J.

questions.text:
A boy throws a ball into air at $45^\circ$ from the horizontal to land it on a roof of a building of height $H$. If the ball attains maximum height in 2 s and lands on the building in 3 s after launch, then value of $H$ is __________ m.
($g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Time to the top: $\dfrac{u_y}{g}=2 \Rightarrow u_y=20$ m/s.
At $t=3$ s: $H=u_yt-\dfrac12gt^2=60-45=15$ m.

questions.text:
Two masses 400 g and 350 g are suspended from the ends of a light string passing over a heavy pulley of radius 2 cm. When released from rest the heavier mass is observed to fall 81 cm in 9 s. The rotational inertia of the pulley is __________ kg.m$^2$.
($g=9.8$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
$s=\dfrac12at^2 \Rightarrow 0.81=\dfrac12a(81) \Rightarrow a=0.02$ m/s$^2$.
$a=\dfrac{(m_1-m_2)g}{m_1+m_2+I/r^2} \Rightarrow 0.75+\dfrac{I}{r^2}=\dfrac{0.05\times9.8}{0.02}=24.5$.
$\dfrac{I}{r^2}=23.75$ kg, so $I=23.75\times(0.02)^2=9.5\times10^{-3}$ kg m$^2$.

questions.text:
Density of water at 4 $^\circ$C and 20 $^\circ$C are 1000 kg/m$^3$ and 998 kg/m$^3$ respectively. The increase in internal energy of 4 kg of water when it is heated from 4 $^\circ$C to 20 $^\circ$C is __________ J.
(specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J / kg. and 1 atmospheric pressure = $10^5$ Pa)
questions.sol:
Taking the specific heat as 4.2 kJ kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$: $Q=4\times4200\times16=268800$ J.
Work done by the water: $W=p\Delta V=10^5\left(\dfrac4{998}-\dfrac4{1000}\right)\approx0.8$ J.
$\Delta U=Q-W=268800-0.8=268799.2$ J.

questions.text: A brass wire of length 2 m and radius 1 mm at 27 $^\circ$C is held taut between two rigid supports. Initially it was cooled to a temperature of $-43$ $^\circ$C creating a tension $T$ in the wire. The temperature to which the wire has to be cooled in order to increase the tension in it to $1.4T$, is __________ $^\circ$C.
questions.sol:
Thermal tension $T=YA\alpha\,\Delta\theta$, so $T\propto\Delta\theta$.
Cooling by $70^\circ$C gives $T$, so $1.4T$ needs $98^\circ$C of cooling: $27-98=-71^\circ$C.

questions.text: A cylindrical block of mass $M$ and area of cross section $A$ is floating in a liquid of density $\rho$ and with its axis vertical. When depressed a little and released the block starts oscillating. The period of oscillation is __________.
questions.sol:
Pushing the block down by $x$ adds buoyancy $\rho Agx$ upwards, so the restoring force constant is $k=\rho Ag$.
$T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{k}}=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{\rho Ag}}$.

questions.text:
The electrostatic potential in a charged spherical region of radius $r$ varies as $V=ar^3+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. The total charge in the sphere of unit radius is $\alpha\times\pi a\epsilon_0$. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
(permittivity of vacuum is $\epsilon_0$)
questions.sol:
$E=-\dfrac{dV}{dr}=-3ar^2$ (radial).
Gauss's law at $r=1$: $q=4\pi\epsilon_0r^2E=4\pi\epsilon_0(-3a)=-12\pi a\epsilon_0$, so $\alpha=-12$.

questions.text: Two resistors of 100 $\Omega$ each are connected in series with a 9 V battery. A voltmeter of 400 $\Omega$ resistance is connected to measure the voltage drop across one of the resistors. The voltmeter reading is __________ V.
questions.sol:
100 $\Omega$ in parallel with 400 $\Omega$ gives 80 $\Omega$.
Reading $=9\times\dfrac{80}{80+100}=4$ V.

Power factor $=\dfrac RZ=0.6=\dfrac{6}{10}$, so $\alpha=6$.

questions.text: There are three co-centric conducting spherical shells $A$, $B$ and $C$ of radii $a$, $b$ and $c$ respectively $(c>b>a)$ and they are charged with charge $q_1$, $q_2$ and $q_3$ respectively. The potentials of the spheres $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively, are :
questions.sol:
A shell of charge $q$ and radius $R$ gives potential $\dfrac{q}{4\pi\epsilon_0R}$ inside and $\dfrac{q}{4\pi\epsilon_0r}$ outside.
$V_A$: inside all three, $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\dfrac{q_1}a+\dfrac{q_2}b+\dfrac{q_3}c\right)$.
$V_B$: outside A, on B, inside C, $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\dfrac{q_1+q_2}b+\dfrac{q_3}c\right)$.
$V_C$: outside all, $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\cdot\dfrac{q_1+q_2+q_3}c$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Three charges $+2q$, $+3q$ and $-4q$ are situated at $(0, -3a)$, $(2a, 0)$ and $(-2a, 0)$ respectively in the $xy$ plane. The resultant dipole moment about origin is __________.
questions.sol: $\vec p=\sum q_i\vec r_i=2q(-3a\hat j)+3q(2a\hat i)-4q(-2a\hat i)=14qa\hat i-6qa\hat j=2qa\left(7\hat i-3\hat j\right)$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-IList-II
A. Radio-waveI. is produced by Magnetron valve
B. Micro-waveII. due to change in the vibrational modes of atoms
C. Infrared-waveIII. due to inner shell electrons moving from higher energy level to lower energy level
D. X-rayIV. due to rapid acceleration of electrons
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Radio: rapid acceleration of electrons in aerials (IV). Microwaves: magnetron valve (I).
Infrared: vibrations of atoms and molecules (II). X-rays: inner-shell electron transitions (III).
A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: An unpolarised light is incident at an interface of two dielectric media having refractive indices of 2 (incident medium) and $2\sqrt{3}$ (medium) respectively. To satisfy the condition that reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other, the angle of incidence is __________.
questions.sol: Reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular at the Brewster angle: $\tan i_B=\dfrac{n_2}{n_1}=\dfrac{2\sqrt3}{2}=\sqrt3$, so $i_B=60^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a microscope of tube length 10 cm two convex lenses are arranged with focal length of 2 cm and 5 cm. Total magnification obtained with this system for normal adjustment is $(5)^k$. The value of $k$ is __________.
questions.sol: Normal adjustment: $m=\dfrac{L}{f_o}\cdot\dfrac{D}{f_e}=\dfrac{10}{2}\times\dfrac{25}{5}=25=5^2$, so $k=2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The exit surface of a prism with refractive index $n$ is coated with a material having refractive index $\dfrac{n}{2}$. When this prism is set for minimum angle of deviation, it exactly meets the condition of critical angle. The prism angle is __________.
questions.sol:
At minimum deviation the angle inside at the exit face is $r_2=\dfrac A2$.
Critical condition at the exit face: $n\sin\dfrac A2=\dfrac n2\sin90^\circ \Rightarrow \sin\dfrac A2=\dfrac12 \Rightarrow A=60^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: For all elements, greater the mass of the nucleus, greater is the binding energy per nucleon.
Statement II: For all elements, nuclei with less binding energy per nucleon transforms to nuclei with greater binding energy per nucleon.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is false: binding energy per nucleon peaks near $A\approx56$ and falls for heavier nuclei.
Statement II is true: nuclear changes (fission of heavy nuclei, fusion of light ones) release energy by moving towards higher binding energy per nucleon.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two electrons are moving in orbits of two hydrogen like atoms with speeds $3\times10^5$ m/s and $2.5\times10^5$ m/s respectively. If the radii of these orbits are nearly same then the possible order of energy states are __________ respectively.
questions.sol:
Bohr model: $r\propto\dfrac{n^2}{Z}$ and $v\propto\dfrac Zn$.
Equal radii means $Z\propto n^2$, so $v\propto\dfrac{n^2}{n}=n$.
$\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}=\dfrac{3}{2.5}=\dfrac65$: the states 6 and 5.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A voltage regulating circuit consisting of Zener diode, having break-down voltage of 10 V and maximum power dissipation of 0.4 W, is operated at 15 V. The approximate value of protective resistance in this circuit is __________ $\Omega$.
questions.sol:
Maximum Zener current $=\dfrac{0.4}{10}=0.04$ A.
Protective resistance $=\dfrac{15-10}{0.04}=125\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In the given figure the blocks $A$, $B$ and $C$ weigh 4 kg, 6 kg and 8 kg respectively. The co-efficient of sliding friction between any two surfaces is 0.5. The force $\vec{F}$ required to slide the block $C$ with constant speed is __________ N. (Use $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.note: The official final key gives 210, which assumes block A is held at rest. The figure shows no support for A; if A simply rides on B, the force works out to 190 N. The key is followed.
questions.sol:
B and C are joined by the cord over the pulley, so when C moves left B moves right. The key's value treats A as held at rest (as in the standard form of this problem, where A is fixed to the wall), so friction acts at every surface.
A on B: $0.5\times40=20$ N. B on C: $0.5\times(40+60)=50$ N. Ground on C: $0.5\times180=90$ N.
For B: $T=20+50=70$ N.
For C: $F=T+50+90=70+50+90=210$ N.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Sixty four rain drops of radius 1 mm each falling down with a terminal velocity of 10 cm/s coalesce to form a bigger drop. The terminal velocity of bigger drop is __________ cm/s.
questions.sol:
Volume is conserved: $R^3=64r^3 \Rightarrow R=4r$.
Terminal velocity $\propto r^2$, so $v=16\times10=160$ cm/s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A gas of certain mass filled in a closed cylinder at a pressure of 3.23 kPa has temperature 50 $^\circ$C. The gas is now heated to double its temperature. The modified pressure is __________ Pa.
questions.note: The official final key (3730 Pa) doubles the Celsius temperature (50 $^\circ$C to 100 $^\circ$C). Doubling the kelvin temperature (323 K to 646 K) would give 6460 Pa. The key is followed.
questions.sol:
At constant volume $p\propto T$ (in kelvin). The key reads ''double its temperature'' as 50 $^\circ$C to 100 $^\circ$C, i.e. 323 K to 373 K.
$p=3230\times\dfrac{373}{323}=3730$ Pa.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A short bar magnet placed with its axis at $30^\circ$ with an external field of 800 Gauss, experiences a torque of 0.016 N.m. The work done in moving it from most stable to most unstable position is $\alpha\times10^{-3}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.sol:
$\tau=mB\sin30^\circ \Rightarrow m=\dfrac{0.016}{0.08\times0.5}=0.4$ A m$^2$ (800 G $=0.08$ T).
Work from $\theta=0$ to $\theta=180^\circ$: $W=2mB=2\times0.4\times0.08=0.064=64\times10^{-3}$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider a mixture 'X' which is made by dissolving 0.4 mol of $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5SO_4]Br}$ and 0.4 mol of $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4}$ in water to make 4 L of solution. When 2 L of mixture 'X' is allowed to react with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$, it forms precipitate 'Y'. The rest 2 L of mixture 'X' reacts with excess $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$ to form precipitate 'Z'. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
questions.sol:
Each 2 L portion holds 0.2 mol of each complex.
Only the ionisable (outer-sphere) ions precipitate: $\mathrm{Br^-}$ of $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5SO_4]Br}$ gives 0.2 mol AgBr (Y), and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ of $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4}$ gives 0.2 mol $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$ (Z).
So 0.2 mol of Z is formed.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I
Isothermal process for ideal gas system		List-II
Work done $(V_f>V_i)$
A. Reversible expansionI. $w=0$
B. Free expansionII. $w=-nRT\ln\dfrac{V_f}{V_i}$
C. Irreversible expansionIII. $w=-p_{ex}(V_f-V_i)$
D. Irreversible compressionIV. $w=-p_{ex}(V_i-V_f)$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Reversible isothermal expansion: $w=-nRT\ln\dfrac{V_f}{V_i}$ (II). Free expansion against zero pressure: $w=0$ (I).
Irreversible expansion against $p_{ex}$: $w=-p_{ex}(V_f-V_i)$ (III). Irreversible compression: the remaining form (IV).
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

questions.text:
Given below are statements about some molecules/ions.
Identify the CORRECT statements.
A. The dipole moment value of $\mathrm{NF_3}$ is higher than that of $\mathrm{NH_3}$.
B. The dipole moment value of $\mathrm{BeH_2}$ is zero.
C. The bond order of $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{F_2}$ is same.
D. The formal charge on the central oxygen atom of ozone is $-1$.
E. In $\mathrm{NO_2}$, all the three atoms satisfy the octet rule, hence it is very stable.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: false; in $\mathrm{NF_3}$ the lone-pair moment opposes the bond moments, so $\mu(\mathrm{NF_3})<\mu(\mathrm{NH_3})$.
B: true; linear $\mathrm{BeH_2}$ has zero dipole moment. C: true; both have bond order 1.
D: false; the central O of ozone carries $+1$. E: false; $\mathrm{NO_2}$ is an odd-electron molecule.
B and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
A solution is prepared by dissolving 0.3 g of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute 'A' of molar mass 60 g mol$^{-1}$ and 0.9 g of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute 'B' of molar mass 180 g mol$^{-1}$ in 100 mL $\mathrm{H_2O}$ at 27$^\circ$C. Osmotic pressure of the solution will be
[Given: R = 0.082 L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
'W' g of a non-volatile electrolyte solid solute of molar mass 'M' g mol$^{-1}$ when dissolved in 100 mL water, decreases vapour pressure of water from 640 mm Hg to 600 mm Hg. If aqueous solution of the electrolyte boils at 375 K and $K_b$ for water is 0.52 K kg mol$^{-1}$, then the mole fraction of the electrolyte solute $(x_2)$ in the solution can be expressed as
(Given : density of water = 1 g/mL and boiling point of water = 373 K)
questions.sol:
Relative lowering: $\dfrac{40}{640}=\dfrac1{16}=i\,x_2$.
Boiling point: $2=i\times0.52\times\dfrac{W/M}{0.1} \Rightarrow i=\dfrac{2M}{5.2W}$.
$x_2=\dfrac{1}{16i}=\dfrac{5.2W}{32M}=\dfrac{1.3}{8}\times\dfrac WM$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
At 27 $^\circ$C in presence of a catalyst, activation energy of a reaction is lowered by 10 kJ mol$^{-1}$. The logarithm of ratio of $\dfrac{k(\text{catalysed})}{k(\text{uncatalysed})}$ is....
(Consider that the frequency factor for both the reactions is same)
questions.sol: With the same $A$: $\log\dfrac{k_c}{k_u}=\dfrac{\Delta E_a}{2.303RT}=\dfrac{10000}{2.303\times8.314\times300}\approx1.741$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$\mathrm{A\rightarrow D}$ is an endothermic reaction occurring in three steps (elementary).
(i) $\mathrm{A\rightarrow B}$ $\Delta H_i=+$ve
(ii) $\mathrm{B\rightarrow C}$ $\Delta H_{ii}=-$ve
(iii) $\mathrm{C\rightarrow D}$ $\Delta H_{iii}=-$ve
Which of the following graphs between potential energy (y-axis) vs reaction coordinate (x-axis) correctly represents the reaction profile of $\mathrm{A\rightarrow D}$?
questions.sol:
The profile needs three humps (three elementary steps) with B above A, C below B, D below C, and D still above A (overall endothermic).
Graph (2) is the only one with this sequence of levels: in (1) D lies above C, in (3) B lies below A, and in (4) C lies above B.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: K > Mg > Al > B is the correct order in terms of metallic character.
Statement II: Atomic radius is always greater than the ionic radius for any element.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is true: metallic character falls across a period and rises down a group, giving K > Mg > Al > B.
Statement II is false: anions are larger than their parent atoms (e.g. $\mathrm{Cl^-}>\mathrm{Cl}$).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Among the following, the CORRECT combinations are
A. $\mathrm{IF_3\rightarrow}$ T-shaped ($sp^3d$)
B. $\mathrm{IF_5\rightarrow}$ Square pyramidal ($sp^3d^2$)
C. $\mathrm{IF_7\rightarrow}$ Pentagonal bipyramidal ($sp^3d^3$)
D. $\mathrm{ClO_4^-\rightarrow}$ Square planar ($sp^2d$)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{IF_3}$: 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs, $sp^3d$, T-shaped (A correct).
$\mathrm{IF_5}$: 5 + 1, $sp^3d^2$, square pyramidal (B correct). $\mathrm{IF_7}$: 7 + 0, $sp^3d^3$, pentagonal bipyramidal (C correct).
$\mathrm{ClO_4^-}$ is tetrahedral ($sp^3$), so D is wrong.
A, B and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Hybridisation, shape and spin only magnetic moment of $\mathrm{K_3[Co(CO_3)_3]}$ is $sp^3d^2$, octahedral and 4.9 BM respectively.
Statement II: Geometry, hybridisation and spin only magnetic moment values (BM) of the ions $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{[MnBr_4]^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ respectively are square planar, tetrahedral, octahedral; $dsp^2$, $sp^3$, $sp^3d^2$ and 0, 5.9, 4.9.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.note: Official final key: options (1) and (4) are both accepted.
questions.sol:
Statement II is true: $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ ($d^8$, strong field) is square planar, $dsp^2$, 0 BM; $\mathrm{[MnBr_4]^{2-}}$ ($d^5$) is tetrahedral, $sp^3$, 5 unpaired, 5.9 BM; $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ ($d^6$, weak field) is octahedral, $sp^3d^2$, 4 unpaired, 4.9 BM.
Statement I depends on whether carbonate is treated as a weak-field ligand: a high-spin Co(III) complex would be $sp^3d^2$ with 4.9 BM (true), while carbonate is usually treated as giving low-spin, $d^2sp^3$, diamagnetic Co(III) (false).
So option (4) (or option (1) on the weak-field view); the final key accepts both.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The number of paramagnetic species among $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[TiF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ and $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ is 3.
Statement II: $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]<K_3[Fe(CN)_6]<[Fe(H_2O)_6]\,SO_4.H_2O<[Fe(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}$ is the correct order in terms of number of unpaired electron(s) present in the complexes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ (4 unpaired), $\mathrm{[TiF_6]^{3-}}$ ($d^1$) and $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ (low-spin $d^5$, 1 unpaired) are paramagnetic; $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ ($d^0$) is not. Three: true.
Statement II: unpaired electrons 0 (low-spin $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$), 1 (low-spin $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$), 4 (high-spin $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$), 5 (high-spin $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$): true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
A student is given one compound among the following compounds that gives positive test with Tollen's reagent.
The compound is :
questions.sol:
C is a cyclic hemiacetal (2-hydroxytetrahydrofuran). In solution it opens to 4-hydroxybutanal, whose free CHO group reduces Tollens' reagent.
A is a cyclic acetal and B and D are an ether and an alcohol; none of them gives a free aldehyde.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Arrange the following carbanions in the decreasing order of stability.
I. $p-\mathrm{Br-C_6H_4-\overset{\ominus}{\ddot{C}}H_2}$
II. $\mathrm{C_6H_5-\overset{\ominus}{\ddot{C}}H_2}$
III. $p-\mathrm{CH_3O-C_6H_4-\overset{\ominus}{\ddot{C}}H_2}$
IV. $p-\mathrm{CHO-C_6H_4-\overset{\ominus}{\ddot{C}}H_2}$
V. $p-\mathrm{CH_3-C_6H_4-\overset{\ominus}{\ddot{C}}H_2}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Electron-withdrawing groups stabilise a benzylic carbanion; electron-donating groups destabilise it.
p-CHO ($-M$) stabilises most; p-Br ($-I$) stabilises a little; H is the reference; p-$\mathrm{CH_3}$ (+I, hyperconjugation) destabilises; p-$\mathrm{OCH_3}$ (+M) destabilises most.
IV > I > II > V > III.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Arrange the following alkenes in decreasing order of stability.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
I is tetrasubstituted (2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene), III is trisubstituted (2-methylbut-2-ene), II is trans-but-2-ene and IV is cis-but-2-ene.
More alkyl groups on the C=C give more hyperconjugation, and trans is more stable than cis (less steric strain).
I > III > II > IV.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: 'C $-$ Cl' bond is stronger in $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-Cl}$ than $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-Cl}$
Statement II: The given optically active molecule, shown below, on hydrolysis gives a solution that can rotate the plane polarized light.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is true: in vinyl chloride the C-Cl bond has partial double-bond character (resonance) and the carbon is $sp^2$, so the bond is shorter and stronger.
Statement II is false: the tertiary benzylic chloride hydrolyses by $S_N1$ through a planar carbocation, giving a racemic alcohol that does not rotate plane-polarised light.

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I
Chloro derivative		List-II
Example
A. Vinyl ChlorideI. $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2Cl}$
B. Benzyl ChlorideII. $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(Cl)CH_3}$
C. Alkyl ChlorideIII. $\mathrm{CH_2=CHCl}$
D. Allyl ChlorideIV. $\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH(Cl)-CH_3}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Vinyl: Cl on an $sp^2$ C=C carbon, $\mathrm{CH_2=CHCl}$ (III). Benzyl: Cl on a carbon next to the ring, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH(Cl)CH_3}$ (IV).
Alkyl: 2-chloropropane (II). Allyl: Cl on the carbon next to C=C, $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2Cl}$ (I).

Numerical value of [molar mass of x + molar mass of y] is ____.

(B) Benzoic acid + $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ gives sodium benzoate, water and carbon dioxide: y = $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (44 g mol$^{-1}$).

questions.text: The correct stability order of the following diazonium salts is
questions.sol:
Arenediazonium ions are stabilised by electron donation into the ring and destabilised by electron withdrawal.
p-$\mathrm{OCH_3}$ (+M) stabilises most; the unsubstituted salt comes next; p-CN and then p-$\mathrm{NO_2}$ (stronger $-M$) destabilise.

questions.text: A hydroxy compound (X) with molar mass 122 g mol$^{-1}$ is acetylated with acetic anhydride, using a large excess of the reagent ensuring complete acetylation of all hydroxyl groups. The product obtained has a molar mass of 290 g mol$^{-1}$. The number of hydroxyl groups present in compound (X) is:
questions.sol:
Each acetylation replaces $-$OH by $-\mathrm{OCOCH_3}$, adding $42$ g mol$^{-1}$.
Number of OH groups $=\dfrac{290-122}{42}=4$.

questions.text: Consider three metal chlorides x, y and z, where x is water soluble at room temperature, y is sparingly soluble in water at room temperature and z is soluble in hot water. x, y and z are respectively
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{CuCl_2}$ dissolves readily in water; AgCl is only very sparingly soluble; $\mathrm{PbCl_2}$ is sparingly soluble in cold water but dissolves in hot water (the basis of separating $\mathrm{Pb^{2+}}$ in group I of salt analysis).
So x, y, z = $\mathrm{CuCl_2}$, AgCl, $\mathrm{PbCl_2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: X and Y are the number of electrons involved, respectively during the oxidation of $\mathrm{I^-}$ to $\mathrm{I_2}$ and $\mathrm{S^{2-}}$ to S by acidified $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$. The value of X + Y is ____.
questions.note: The official final key gives 12, counting the electrons transferred in each balanced reaction with one dichromate ion (6 + 6). Counting per $\mathrm{I_2}$ and per S atom formed would give 2 + 2 = 4. The key is followed.
questions.sol:
Each $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ takes 6 electrons ($\mathrm{2Cr^{6+}\to2Cr^{3+}}$), so the balanced reactions transfer 6 electrons each:
$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}+6I^-+14H^+\rightarrow2Cr^{3+}+3I_2+7H_2O}$ (X = 6)
$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}+3S^{2-}+14H^+\rightarrow2Cr^{3+}+3S+7H_2O}$ (Y = 6)
X + Y = 12.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
In Dumas method for estimation of nitrogen, 0.50 g of an organic compound gave 70 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K and 715 mm pressure. The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is ____ %.
(Aqueous tension at 300 K is 15 mm).
questions.sol:
Pressure of dry $\mathrm{N_2}=715-15=700$ mm.
Volume at STP $=70\times\dfrac{700}{760}\times\dfrac{273}{300}\approx58.7$ mL.
Mass of $\mathrm{N_2}=\dfrac{58.7}{22400}\times28\approx0.0734$ g, so % N $=\dfrac{0.0734}{0.50}\times100\approx14.7\approx15$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: The hydrogen spectrum consists of several spectral lines in Lyman series ($L_1$, $L_2$, $L_3$...; $L_1$ has lowest energy among Lyman series). Similarly it consists of several spectral lines in Balmer series ($B_1$, $B_2$, $B_3$ ... ; $B_1$ has lowest energy among Balmer lines). The energy of $L_1$ is $x$ times the energy of $B_1$. The value of $x$ is __________ $\times10^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
$L_1$: $n=2\to1$, $E\propto1-\dfrac14=\dfrac34$. $B_1$: $n=3\to2$, $E\propto\dfrac14-\dfrac19=\dfrac5{36}$.
$x=\dfrac{3/4}{5/36}=\dfrac{27}{5}=5.4=54\times10^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider two Group IV metal ions $\mathrm{X^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Y^{2+}}$.
A solution containing 0.01 M $\mathrm{X^{2+}}$ and 0.01 M $\mathrm{Y^{2+}}$ is saturated with $\mathrm{H_2S}$. The pH at which the metal sulphide YS will form as a precipitate is ____. (Nearest integer)
(Given: $K_{sp}$ (XS) $=1\times10^{-22}$ at 25$^\circ$C, $K_{sp}$ (YS) $=4\times10^{-16}$ at 25$^\circ$C, $\mathrm{[H_2S]}=0.1$M in solution, $K_{a1}\times K_{a2}\,(\mathrm{H_2S})=1.0\times10^{-21}$, log 2 = 0.30, log 3 = 0.48, log 5 = 0.70)
questions.sol:
YS precipitates when $\mathrm{[S^{2-}]}\ge\dfrac{4\times10^{-16}}{0.01}=4\times10^{-14}$ M.
$\mathrm{[S^{2-}]}=\dfrac{K_{a1}K_{a2}\mathrm{[H_2S]}}{\mathrm{[H^+]}^2}=\dfrac{10^{-22}}{\mathrm{[H^+]}^2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{[H^+]}^2=2.5\times10^{-9}$, $\mathrm{[H^+]}=5\times10^{-5}$ M.
pH $=5-\log5=4.3\approx4$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Electricity is passed through an acidic solution of $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ till all the $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ was exhausted, leading to the deposition of 300 mg of Cu metal. However, a current of 600 mA was continued to pass through the same solution for another 28 minutes by keeping the total volume of the solution fixed at 200 mL. The total volume of oxygen evolved at STP during the entire process is ____ mL. (Nearest integer)
[Given:
$\mathrm{Cu^{2+}(aq)+2e^-\rightarrow Cu(s)}$ $E^\circ_{red}=+0.34$ V
$\mathrm{O_2(g)+4H^++4e^-\rightarrow2H_2O}$ $E^\circ_{red}=+1.23$ V
